title: Onramp Landingpad Standup — Morning Sync
body:
Date: 2028-01-09
Attendees: Priya Nambiar (owner), Evan McClure, Maya Chen, Lucas Ortega, Hannah Stein, Samir Rao (on call for Veridian), Natalia (customer PM, CobaltHealth, joined briefly)
Duration: 25m standup (quick morning pulse)

Purpose: quick health/status sync for active onramp customers running through Landingpad (initial infra + integration window). Capture blockers, sequencing, and immediate escalation items for SRE/Product if needed.

Agenda:
- Quick status per customer (green/amber/red)
- Items needing SRE/Infra support this week
- Rollout gating checks and quality flags
- Action items and owners

High level summary:
- Overall cohort: 6 active customers in week-1/2 of onramp. Two amber (CobaltHealth, Tidewater) due to infra config and auth handshake flakiness. One red briefly (Veridian) but mitigated with a fallback model policy. Remaining are green-moving.
- Short-term risk: certificate rotation issue (internal CA) may recur during region failovers; SRE follow-up required.
- Decision: enable temporary canary routing to model-variant v2a for customers with intermittent KV-cache corruption until patch deploys (see PR #412).

Per-customer notes:
1) Veridian Health — STATUS: AMBER -> briefly RED on 2028-01-07, stabilized
- What happened: during load test on Friday they hit an edge case in prefix cache invalidation; responses contained stale context for ~10 users. Observed ~0.4% error rate, user-facing tickets created by Veridian.
- Mitigation: rolled fallback routing to model-variant v2a (lower batching aggressiveness) at 23:10 PST; issue confined.
- Current work: runtime patch queued (SE-2684) to tighten cache eviction heuristics. Patch in review, ops PR #412 for deployment plan.
- Open blockers: need a KV-cache warmup job to run pre-traffic in Landingpad (JIRA: PS-3912). SRE help needed to schedule cron in staging.
- Owner & ETA: Samir Rao + Evan — staging job spec by 2028-01-11; deploy to staging 2028-01-13; customer-facing postmortem draft due 2028-01-15.

2) CobaltHealth — STATUS: AMBER
- Symptoms: intermittent 401s on private-deploy auth exchange when regional failover occurs. Failure mode seems tied to short TTL on internal service token plus a race on refresh.
- Recent triage: Maya reproduced locally with simulated failovers; confirmed token refresh window mismatch.
- Proposed fix: increase refresh buffer and add idempotent refresh path in handshake. Code change scoped, needs security review (token lifecycle consequences).
- Blocker: Security review queue (~2 days). Also need one more telemetry event to trace refresh latency (instrumentation task).
- Owner & ETA: Maya Chen (code) + Hannah (sec touchpoint) — aim to have patch and telemetry in staging by 2028-01-14.

3) Tidewater — STATUS: GREEN/AMBER watch
- On track with routing and production smoke. Slight cost spike observed from unexpectedly high batch sizes on long-sequence tests — unit economics flagged by Optimize team.
- Action: enable dynamic batching caps for Tidewater's route (conservative cap) and run a 24h smoke to confirm cost baseline.
- Owner & ETA: Lucas Ortega to flip config in Landingpad by 2028-01-10; monitor and report 2028-01-12.

4) Lighthouse (pilot) — STATUS: GREEN
- No significant issues. Canary rollout completed for model v3b, user acceptance tests passed.
- Small doc updates requested for dev onboarding (quickstart snippets).
- Owner: Priya (doc pass), ETA 2028-01-12.

5) NovaPay — STATUS: GREEN
- Integration mostly infra-only (network peering + KMS). Peering approved; KMS key policy QA in progress.
- Owner: Evan; expect go-live for E2E tests 2028-01-16.

Cross-team items / escalations:
- SRE: certificate rotation / internal CA — intermittent failures noted when landing new EC2 instances in the eu-west region during rolling upgrades. Need a hardening window. Action: SRE runbook sync with SE next Tuesday 2028-01-11.
- Security: CobaltHealth token refresh path requires security signoff. Hannah to triage and expedite review.
- Product: decision to allow temporary canary fallback (v2a) for customers impacted by cache invalidation. Product wants a quality metric threshold for rollback (error rate < 0.05% for 24h).
- Optimize team: Tidewater cost anomaly — request to run a model of predicted per-token cost under dynamic batching changes. Lucas to share metrics link (internal dashboard) by EOD 2028-01-09.

Action items (quick list):
- SE-2684: finalize cache eviction patch & tests — Owner: Evan McClure — Due: 2028-01-11
- PS-3912: spec and schedule KV-cache warmup job in staging — Owner: Samir Rao — Due: 2028-01-11
- CobaltHealth auth fix + telemetry: implement and request security review — Owner: Maya Chen — Due: 2028-01-13
- Enable conservative batching cap for Tidewater route; run 24h smoke — Owner: Lucas Ortega — Done-by: 2028-01-10
- Landingpad docs quickstart update (Lighthouse onboarding) — Owner: Priya Nambiar — Due: 2028-01-12
- SRE runbook sync meeting invite & agenda — Owner: Hannah Stein — Scheduled: 2028-01-11

Notes to self / open questions (informal):
- Should we short-circuit canary to use v2a by default for all customers with active onramp until the patch lands? Product leaning against broad switching; prefer targeted routing per-customer.
- Are there any customers running on Dedicated that need different KV-warmup semantics? (Samir to surface list)
- Confirm whether billing alerts should be muted during Tidewater smoke to avoid noisy paging — ask Optimize.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Targeted canary fallback only for customers that hit >0.2% error in last 6h (manual toggle).
- Proceed with KV-cache warmup job design; do not ship to prod until canary proves stable.

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Quick sync Wed 2028-01-11 09:15 PST to review staging results and SRE runbook notes. If any customer flips red, escalate immediately via #se-onramp and page SRE (pager duty policy remains).

Attachments / refs: see linked_artifacts (JIRA tickets, PR #412, Confluence runbook).

End of notes.

Informal / scratch: lots of shorthand in chat thread — will collate into postmortem once SE-2684 lands.
